rows.text: | Tool reference is a generated projection of the registry | 2 | The new test `tools_reference_matches_registry` in `crates/cli/tests/protocol.rs` renders, from `Tools::definitions()` (name, description, input properties with type and required, output top-level properties) in registry order, the block between `<!-- tools-reference:begin -->` and `<!-- tools-reference:end -->` in `docs/TOOLS.md`. It asserts byte equality and prints a diff on failure; `PURRASSIST_BLESS=1` rewrites it and panics if `CI` is set, following the `recovery_goldens` precedent. Each generated entry shows the MCP `tools/call` name, `purrassist call NAME --root DIR < args.json`, and its example file when one exists. Hand-written per-tool narrative (moved from the README) sits outside the block, under `### <tool>` headings. `check-docs.py` counts the hand-written `### <tool>` headings outside the generated block, against the tool names inside it (the block itself is byte-pinned by the Rust test). There must be exactly one heading per name, and no headings for unknown names. |
rows.author: paudley
